items.title: Trump's showmanship distracts from all that was riding on today's address
items.description: Donald Trump's showmanship and supreme confidence can easily distract from the fact that he had a lot riding on his State of the Union address on Tuesday.

items.title: Two charged over alleged abduction and death of Sydney grandfather
items.description: Two men have been charged over the alleged kidnapping and death of Sydney grandfather Chris Baghsarian.

items.title: Australian diplomats' families offered evacuation over Iran threat
items.description: The Australian government offers to evacuate the families of Australian diplomats and officials from some of its missions in the Middle East, with the prospect of US strikes on Iran leaving the region on high alert.

items.title: First-home buyer affordability no longer just a Sydney problem
items.description: The Australian dream of home ownership is becoming an increasingly unrealistic goal for young Australians, new research from Domain has found, with repayments on an entry-level house now averaging almost half a couple's combined income.

items.title: Australian jailed for seven years for 'betraying' the US
items.description: A judge in Washington has sentenced Australian man Peter Williams to 87 months in prison for selling sensitive information to a Russian broker.

items.title: 'Doesn't the case have to fail?': Judge interrupts closing statement in Coles trial
items.description: The judge overseeing a bombshell federal court case has made a stunning intervention as the consumer watchdog makes closing arguments.

items.title: Axed Biennale artist to take not one but two huge installations to Venice
items.description: Last year, Khaled Sabsabi was dumped from the Venice Biennale to avoid "divisive debate". Now, he announces his work will feature in both the main exhibition and the Australia Pavilion.

items.title: Controversial NT administrator apologises over 'hurt' from social media posts
items.description: Just a day before being sworn in as the Northern Territory's new representative for King Charles III, NT Administrator David Connolly has apologised over a social media furore.

items.title: Childhood education student had abuse material on phone, ABF alleges
items.description: A Chinese national intending to study early childhood education in Australia has had his visa cancelled after Australian Border Force officers checked his baggage at Adelaide Airport and allegedly found "21 videos deemed to be child abuse material".

items.title: Security threat prompting PM evacuation linked to intimidation of Chinese dancers
items.description: The prime minister was forced to evacuate the Lodge last night due to a bomb threat linked to performances in Australia by a classical Chinese dance and music group that is banned in China.

items.title: Alleged bomb threat against Gold Coast theatre over Chinese dance group
items.description: Shen Yun has been the subject of several threats, including one against Australia's prime minister on Monday.

items.title: 'Unbelievable amount of water': Towns receive over 200mm in 24 hours
items.description: Some pastoralists have already recorded 215mm of rain overnight, with the coming days forecast to bring an additional 100mm in some parts north-east of SA and far west NSW.

items.title: Teenager first in SA to be prosecuted under new deepfake laws
items.description: A suppression order has been lifted on the identity of the first South Australian man to be prosecuted for allegedly creating and sharing sexually explicit deepfake images.

items.title: WiseTech to slash 2,000 jobs as AI ends era of 'manually writing code'
items.description: The company says almost one third of staff across 40 countries would be affected by the redundancies as a move towards AI sees a reshaping of its workforce.

items.title: What is duty sex and how do you stop having it?
items.description: Obligatory or duty sex is most common in long-term relationships, but can also happen in casual relationships where sex is the basis of the connection.

items.title: Poet takes home $125,000 for 'uncompromising' second collection
items.description: Eveyln Araluen has taken out the top award at the Victorian Premier's Literary Awards for The Rot, the follow up to her award-winning debut, Dropbear.

items.title: Colin was on 32 medications. A pharmacist home visit changed his life
items.description: Pharmacists are calling for more funding and caps to be removed from a long-running government program that helps patients avoid hospital.

items.title: Shark cull and swimming ban to resume after fatal attack in New Caledonia
items.description: New Caledonian authorities ban beach swimming and resume shark culling despite concern from environmental groups, after a wing foiler is killed in an attack.

items.title: Algal bloom blamed on 'convergence' of events, but ecologist questions finding
items.description: The SA environment minister says preliminary results of an investigation into the causes of the harmful algal bloom back up what scientists had long suspected, but an ecologist who has criticised the government's response says more detail needs to be released.

items.title: Drunk obstetrician's manslaughter sentence 'met expectations', says premier
items.description: WA's political leaders are at odds over the sentence given to obstetrician Rhys Bellinge for a fatal drunken car accident, with Premier Roger Cook backing it and Opposition Leader Basil Zempilas saying it was "on the light side."

items.title: AI expert warns Australia is unprepared for 'supercharged' harms
items.description: Renowned AI expert Toby Walsh has used a National Press Club address to warn the Australian government about what he argues are inadequate approaches to regulating the technology.

items.title: New laws flagged after 'violent' attacks on gay and bisexual Sydney teens
items.description: The New South Wales premier has flagged harsher punishments and new criminal offences in response to gay and bisexual teens being lured online and bashed on camera.

items.title: AFL says umpires' opinion still matters after announcing Brownlow change
items.description: The AFL confirms umpires will be able to access player statistics before casting their votes in a bid to quell any controversy around the Brownlow Medal count.

items.title: Sydney doctor was passport 'delivery boy' for IS-linked families in Syria
items.description: Australian doctor Jamal Rifi has been helping to coordinate a potential repatriation effort from Syria, including by obtaining passports for the families.

items.title: Gold Coast Trump Tower developer was 'uncontactable' after business collapse
items.description: The businessman behind a proposed Trump Tower on the Gold Coast ran a development business that collapsed owing $28 million.
